title: Peter Schmeichel
wiki_lead:
Peter Bolesław Schmeichel (born 18 November 1963) is a Danish former professional footballer who played as a goalkeeper. During eight seasons at English club Manchester United, he won 15 trophies including five Premier League titles, three FA Cups, and captaining the club to victory in the 1999 UEFA Champions League final to complete the treble. Schmeichel also played for the Denmark national team, with which he won the UEFA European Championship in 1992. Regarded as one of the greatest goalkeepers of all time, he was voted the IFFHS World's Best Goalkeeper in 1992 and 1993, while the International Federation of Football History & Statistics ranked Schmeichel among the top 10 goalkeepers of the 20th century.
Born in Gladsaxe, Copenhagen, Schmeichel is 1.93 m (6 ft 4 in) tall and weighed close to 100 kg (220 lb; 15 st 10 lb) during his playing days. A fierce competitor, he often loudly criticised perceived mistakes by his defenders. Unusually for a goalkeeper, he scored 11 goals during his career, including one for the national team. He was also the most capped player for Denmark, playing 129 games between 1987 and 2001, until he was overtaken by Simon Kjær in 2023. In addition to Euro 92, he played for his country at the 1998 FIFA World Cup and three more European Championship tournaments. He captained the national team in 30 matches. He also represented Gladsaxe-Hero, Hvidovre, Brøndby, Sporting CP, Aston Villa and Manchester City in a career that lasted from 1981 until 2003 and yielded 24 trophies.
When he retired, he was near to 1,000 career appearances.
In 2001, Schmeichel won a public poll held by Reuters, in which the majority of the 200,000 participants voted him as the best goalkeeper in history, ahead of Lev Yashin and Gordon Banks. In 2003, Schmeichel was inducted into the English Football Hall of Fame in recognition of his impact on the English game. In March 2004, he was named among the "125 greatest living footballers" on the FIFA 100 list. His son Kasper was also a professional goalkeeper, known for playing for Scottish side Celtic, the Premier League winning iteration of Leicester City and the Denmark national team.

Early life
Peter Bolesław Schmeichel was born on 18 November 1963 in the Søborggård parish of Gladsaxe, Denmark, to Antoni Alexander "Tolek" Schmeichel (1933–2019), a Polish jazz musician, and Inger, a Danish nurse. He held Polish citizenship until November 1971 when he, his father, and his three sisters became Danish citizens.
Schmeichel inherited his middle name – Bolesław – from his great-grandfather. He spent his early years in the town of Buddinge, Copenhagen, and began his football career playing for a team in the adjacent suburb of Høje-Gladsaxe. His first match came on 7 August 1972 at the age of 8. Regarded as one of the greatest goalkeepers in football history, Schmeichel was voted the IFFHS World's Best Goalkeeper for 1992 and 1993. He earned 129 caps for the Denmark national team between 1987 and 2001, captaining the side to a shock victory in the UEFA European Championship 1992 after entering as replacements for Yugoslavia. At club level, he is best known for his tenure with Manchester United from 1991 to 1999, during which he secured five Premier League titles, three FA Cups, one UEFA Champions League (as part of the 1999 Treble), and captained the team in the latter final. Schmeichel retired from playing in 2003 after stints with clubs including Sporting CP, Aston Villa, and Manchester City, where he notably became the first goalkeeper to score a Premier League goal in 2001. Known for his commanding presence, agility, and vocal leadership at 1.96 meters tall, he revolutionized the goalkeeper role with aggressive distribution and shot-stopping prowess.
